triage.note: D12 (postmortem 2026-08-25 §8, interviewer-feedback gap 3): item offsets index `normalized_text`, not the raw filing, and until this case nothing said so to a consumer and nothing let one check it. ADR-026 §a refuses a raw-to-normalized offset map, so the remedy is a CONTRACT — serve the exact text the offsets index, publish a sha that binds the download to the run, and carry the slicing recipe verbatim where a consumer will read it. The check pins all three: LIVE, that `build_view`'s `norm_sha256` is the sha256 of the run's own UTF-8 `normalized_text` and that `normalized_text[start:end]` is byte-for-byte the `text` the API serves for that item, on every spanned item of an HTML-era and a txt-era fixture; LIVE, that the same offsets against the RAW bytes produce something DIFFERENT on every one of those items, so the documented warning is falsifiable rather than decorative; and by allow-list pin, that `/api/normalized/{token}` exists exactly once and that every expression on the path from this run's `normalized_text` to the response body is present WHOLE — what goes into the cache, which slot comes back out, the response, the sha header — plus an `ast` guard that neither `_run` nor `api_normalized` binds `norm` more than once, counted as `Name(ctx=Store)` nodes on the function's parse tree — which covers assignment, augmented assignment, walrus, tuple unpack and for-target, and NOT the rebinding forms that emit no Store node at all: `except X as norm`, `import x as norm`, `def norm`, `global`/`nonlocal norm`, and match-statement capture patterns (PR #54 R6, which demonstrated the match case green). That residue is not chased, and the reason is worth stating plainly: `hit = (hit[0], hit[1], hit[1])` written BEFORE the pinned binding serves the raw filing while every `norm` guard stays satisfied, so no guard on this name can ever be complete. This is the inherent ceiling of allow-list pinning over file text, named here rather than built against. The endpoint itself is unreachable from the harness (importing app.py drags fastapi into the dependency-free unit job, the same constraint check_boilerplate_plumbing works around), so what these pins establish is that the code says the right thing, NOT that FastAPI serves it; that half is unpinned and carries its own debt row. PR #54 R1 is why the wording is this careful: the first version pinned only the two expressions that MENTION `norm` and not where `norm` comes from, so `norm = hit[1]` — the endpoint serving the raw filing under a matching sha header — was green, which is the exact defect the check's own comment called impossible. Five mutations were watched red under the repaired pins and green on revert: `norm = hit[1]`, `norm = (result.get("normalized_text") or "")[:100]`, and a second `norm = hit[1]` after the pinned binding written three ways — on its own line, on the same line after a semicolon, and as `norm, _unused = hit[1], 0`. The last two are PR #54 R4: the guard was a line-anchored regex until then and both were green, which is why it is an `ast` walk now — a regex guard is always one spelling behind, and the property wanted is a Store node, not a line shape. Watched red before implementation on 2026-08-26 with 17 failures: no `/api/normalized` route at all, all four wire pins at 0, all five recipe lines missing from each of README.md and app.py, and `norm_sha256=None` on both fixtures. Two halves were already GREEN in that red run and are here for the future, not for this change: the raw-differs half, which is a property of normalization (it goes red the day normalization becomes the identity, and then the docs get to stop shouting), and the slice-equals-served-text half, which is INV-S2 restated at the API boundary (it goes red the day the view serves a second copy instead of a slice — the drift the contract exists to prevent). What this change made true is the SERVED half: before it, there was no endpoint to perform step 2 against and no sha to perform step 3 with, so the recipe was unwritable, not merely unwritten.

provenance: Created 2026-08-26 for D12. Fixtures are the same HTML-era/txt-era pair `ui-boilerplate-exclusion` uses (msft-2013, ge-1994), chosen so the recipe is pinned across both normalizer paths rather than only the modern one; no fixture was added. The recipe text itself lives in `src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py::RECIPE` and the check requires it to appear exactly once in each of README.md and src/sec10k/web/app.py — app.py's copy is the `/api/normalized/{token}` docstring, which FastAPI serves as that endpoint's OpenAPI description, so the reader with no access to this repo gets the recipe at /docs. Comparison is whitespace-free (`_squash`), because the two copies wrap differently and how a sentence is wrapped carries no information. PR #54 R2 added a sixth doc pin, README-only: the worked snippet's step-4 line, which first shipped as a bare `==` that is false for any item longer than DISPLAY_MAX — aapl-2025 item 1A is 68,162 chars against a 40,000-char display copy, so the published recipe raised AssertionError one line below the fixture it printed. The line is pinned in its prefix form, and that pin is ALL that protects it — PR #54 R5, which falsified this sentence's first version. That version claimed the line was also executed against a truncated item; the comparison written for the claim was `slice_[:len(it["text"])] != it["text"]`, which `build_view` makes identical to a check already in the loop, so it could never fail alone and the truncated-item guard on top of it guarded nothing. Both were deleted rather than reworded. Reverting README.md's line alone is red; co-editing README.md and `SNIPPET_ASSERT` back together is green, and that is the ceiling every allow-list pin in this file has.
